newsitem.title: UK: BA's Hatton warns on cargo margins.
newsitem.headline: BA's Hatton warns on cargo margins.

text.p: All scenarios show that air cargo yields are continously declining and airlines need to do something about maintaining their margins, British Airways Plc World Cargo (BAWC) managing director, Kevin Hatton said.
"If airlines are to catch up and compete with the integrators (eg Federal Express Corp ) the investment has got to come from somewhere," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

He added that at last October's International Air Cargo Association (TIACA) conference in Dubai, one underlying theme had been that,"you can't make investments and achieve quality without receiving payment."

Asked about reports that BAWC was involved in extended discounting on many routes, Hatton replied: "We will do what is right for the business. We want to improve the bottom line. We'll do what is most effective."
Earlier today, Reuters quoted a BAWC spokesman saying the airline was continuing until March 2 many of the cut prices it was offering in January on international cargo routes.
The extension covered 25 North Atlantic routes, 14 southern region routes covering the Middle East, East Africa and the Indian sub-continent, Beijing and 13 European routes.
"The Pacific has been very bullish, very good in the last few months," Hatton added.
